transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Diaz (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Head of ML, Equinox), Lena Ortiz (ML Engineer), Rajiv Menon (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Equinox's current embedding + search stack, QPS/latency requirements, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private fit their compliance needs. They are leaning towards a two-stage retrieval + rerank architecture and want throughput baselines and security docs.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the call, with Jordan our solutions eng. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Samir Gupta: Doing good, thanks. Quick intro from our side - I'm Samir, I run ML for Equinox, Lena's our ML engineer who owns search infra, and Rajiv is our CTO.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi all.
[00:15] Jordan Diaz: Hey team, Jordan here, I'll focus on the technical parts of integrations and benchmarks.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Awesome. The agenda - understand your current vector DB and embedding choices, what you're optimizing for, any security/compliance constraints, then map to Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private and agree next steps.
[00:30] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. We have a pretty tight timeline, looking to pick a vendor by end of month and run a pilot in October.
[00:38] Maya Patel: Great, that'll help prioritize. Samir, can you walk us through current stack and pain points?
[00:45] Samir Gupta: Sure. Right now we use an internal ES cluster with OpenSearch for text search, and Pinecone for dense vector recalls in some experiments. Our embedding model is a homegrown 768-dim model for production but we also test 1536-dim embeddings from a third-party. The pain is two-fold: cost for large dims and inconsistent latency under load. We also want better reranking - right now we do simple cosine similarity and then shuffle through a small transformer reranker but it's costly.
[01:12] Jordan Diaz: When you say inconsistent latency, are you seeing p95 spikes on search queries? QPS?
[01:17] Samir Gupta: Yes, p95 is in the 600-800ms range during peak; QPS is around 120 sustained with spikes to 200. We need sub-300ms p95 for the main product.
[01:27] Lena Ortiz: Also storage costs - 1536 dims blow up our vector store size and we are debating whether to reduce dims to 512 or 128 for the broader index and store higher-dim or full context for rerank.
[01:40] Maya Patel: That's a classic tradeoff - lower dims reduce storage and vector DB cost and improve throughput, but you may lose recall. Many customers do a hybrid approach: 128/512 for initial ANNS recall and then use a higher-capacity reranker or on-the-fly re-embedding for top N.
[01:53] Jordan Diaz: Right, Redwood supports that two-stage flow out of the box. Our Hosted API can serve embeddings and also host rerank models as part of a pipeline; for Dedicated you get predictable throughput and isolation which helps with p95 under high QPS. For Private, you can run everything inside your VPC for compliance.
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: We have SOC2 in progress and need KMS/HSM integration for some customers. Would Private be required?
[02:18] Jordan Diaz: Private is the full customer-managed control plane; we support KMS integrations and can do on-prem if needed. Dedicated sits in a Redwood-managed environment but with reserved capacity and private networking options. Hosted is simpler but has less control over VPC peering unless you opt for a private endpoint.
[02:33] Samir Gupta: For the pilot we want to try Hosted first but we need to validate p95 and cost. If Hosted can't meet p95 we would evaluate Dedicated.
[02:41] Maya Patel: Totally reasonable. Jordan, can you walk through typical latency numbers and what impacts them?
[02:45] Jordan Diaz: Sure. For raw embedding generation on a 512-dim model on our Hosted SKU, median token-to-embedding is ~10-20ms, end-to-end query+ANNS lookup p50 can be ~40-80ms for small top-k, p95 depends on batching and index density. Rerank add-on depends on model size - a small cross-encoder reranker adds ~60-120ms per query if served synchronously, but you can also do asynchronous or precompute rerank features. For Dedicated we can guarantee lower tail with reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies.
[03:21] Lena Ortiz: We're curious about dimensionality - if we drop to 128 dims for initial recall, what drop in recall do you typically see? And how does that compare to 512?
[03:30] Jordan Diaz: It really depends on your data. For dense semantic search tasks, 512 tends to be a good balance; 128 often still works for coarse recall but loses nuance. Many customers do 128 for large cold indices with a 512/1536 reranker on top. Also quantization can help - 8-bit/4-bit quantized embeddings in storage reduce footprint. We can run A/B on your sample data to quantify.
[03:51] Samir Gupta: Good - can you integrate with our Pinecone setup or we'd want to migrate?
[03:57] Jordan Diaz: Redwood can talk to external vector DBs - we have connectors and many customers use Pinecone/Weaviate/OpenSearch for storage and Redwood for embedding + rerank. Alternatively, we can host the vectors in Redwood Dedicated storage for lower overall latency since there's less network hop.
[04:14] Rajiv Menon: If we keep Pinecone, do you have issues with throughput for cross-network calls?
[04:20] Jordan Diaz: Cross-network calls add network latency; typical added latency is 10-40ms depending on region and peering. For high QPS setups we recommend colocated or Dedicated storage so the ANN lookup and rerank are closer.
[04:33] Lena Ortiz: For hybrid search - we use BM25 + embeddings in ES now. How would Redwood's flow look?
[04:40] Jordan Diaz: A common pattern is use the BM25 signal to get a candidate set, merge with ANN recall results, then run a cross-encoder reranker on the union. You can tune weights or train a lightweight ranker that uses both BM25 scores and embedding distances. Redwood supports this architecture and can stream candidates from your ES cluster into the rerank pipeline or do the candidate generation within Redwood if you host the vectors there.
[05:08] Samir Gupta: Our query patterns: many short queries from UI with strict latency; also batch offline similarity jobs. The UI is the priority.
[05:16] Maya Patel: For the UI use-case, p95 matters a lot. Our recommendation is run a pilot with 100k vectors, test 128 and 512 dims, measure p50/p95 under 100-200 QPS with realistic query patterns, and evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated.
[05:29] Rajiv Menon: Agreed. Cost - can you ballpark storage and per-query cost for 512 dims?
[05:35] Jordan Diaz: Ballpark only: storage cost depends on quantization and index type. Raw float32 512-dim vectors are ~2MB per 1000 vectors; quantized/OPQ/compressed indexes reduce that dramatically. For Hosted, expect embedding compute + ANN lookup costs; for Dedicated, you pay for reserved capacity which often lowers per-request cost at scale. We'll send a sample cost sheet with per-100k numbers.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: Any caveats on reranker model - is Redwood hosting models or do we bring our own?
[06:04] Jordan Diaz: Both. You can bring your own reranker model (we support standard model formats) or use Redwood's managed rerank models. If you bring yours, we can optimize inference (quantization, batching) for latency.
[06:18] Samir Gupta: On security, we need to ensure logs/auditability and that embeddings are not retained beyond retention policy - can Redwood provide that?
[06:26] Maya Patel: Yes, we provide configurable data retention, audit logs, and SSO/SAML. For Private/Dedicated we can support stricter network and key management requirements. We'll attach the security pack after this call.
[06:38] Rajiv Menon: About evaluation - do you recommend using off-the-shelf embeddings or our in-house model?
[06:44] Jordan Diaz: Often customers try both: off-the-shelf for baseline (like 1536 models) and your in-house for production if it performs better or has lower compute cost. We can run an eval harness on a labeled set to quantitatively compare.
[06:59] Samir Gupta: Good. For the pilot size we mentioned 100k vectors - retention and GDPR concerns may push us to keep data in our VPC eventually.
[07:09] Maya Patel: Noted. For pilot, Hosted is easiest to start - you can move to Dedicated or Private later.
[07:14] Lena Ortiz: One more question on hybrid search: do you support rerank as a streaming call to reduce perceived latency?
[07:20] Jordan Diaz: We support streaming results; you can stream initial candidates immediately and then patch with reranked results once they arrive. This helps UX when p95 rerank latency is higher.
[07:31] Samir Gupta: That could work. Also, how do you handle model versioning for rerank? We need to A/B test models.
[07:38] Jordan Diaz: Redwood supports model versioning and rollouts - you can do canary traffic, A/B, and automatic fallback to a stable model. The Console has dashboards for cost and latency per model.
[07:49] Rajiv Menon: Ops-wise, if we go Dedicated, what uptime guarantees and SLAs do you offer?
[07:55] Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with an SLA that targets high availability and latency commitments - we'll share the SLA doc. Private gets you more control but SLA specifics depend on deployment.
[08:05] Samir Gupta: OK. For the benchmark, what specific metrics should we capture?
[08:10] Jordan Diaz: p50/p95 latency for retrieval and rerank, end-to-end latency, QPS per worker, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1k queries, and recall@k/F1 for relevance. Also index size and memory usage.
[08:23] Lena Ortiz: We have a labeled set for relevance - we can share that.
[08:27] Samir Gupta: Yes we'll share a 5k labeled test set.
[08:31] Maya Patel: Great. I'll put that in next steps. Jordan, any notes about connectors we should call out?
[08:36] Jordan Diaz: We have connectors for Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, and S3 for bulk ingest. For Pinecone specifically, we can either keep Pinecone as the ANN store or migrate to Redwood-managed index for lower latency. Migration tooling exists to export/import.
[08:52] Rajiv Menon: How long does a migration or pilot typically take?
[08:56] Jordan Diaz: Pilot setup often takes 1-2 weeks once data samples and goals are defined. Full migration depends on data size but we can support phased approaches.
[09:05] Maya Patel: Ok sounds like we have alignment. Quick recap and next steps?
[09:10] Samir Gupta: Pilot in October, sample data and labeled set to be shared, Jordan to run throughput tests and Maya to send pricing/security docs.
[09:20] Maya Patel: Yep. We'll send the security pack and pricing today, Jordan will run an initial benchmark and share by 9/14, and we'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week - does 9/10 or 9/11 work?
[09:32] Lena Ortiz: 9/11 works for us.
[09:35] Rajiv Menon: 9/11 ok.
[09:37] Maya Patel: Great. Any final questions?
[09:40] Samir Gupta: None from me. Thanks everyone.
[09:42] Maya Patel: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with docs and scheduling.
